title: Dependency Graph
concept: The dependency graph maps module relationships — enabling parallel compilation, cycle detection, and build optimization.
why: Understanding the dependency graph explains why some changes trigger massive recompilation while others are instant — and how to structure your code for fast builds.
theory:
## Module Relationships

### Visualizing Dependencies

```sh
# Generate dependency graph
xiom graph --output deps.dot

# Render to image (requires Graphviz)
dot -Tpng deps.dot -o deps.png
```

### Graph Structure

```
main.xi
├── module auth
│   ├── module crypto
│   │   └── module math (stdlib)
│   └── module database
│       └── module sql (external package)
├── module api
│   ├── module auth
│   ├── module json (stdlib)
│   └── module http (external package)
└── module config
```

### Critical Path

The longest chain in the dependency graph determines minimum build time:

```
math → crypto → auth → api → main
```

Changes to `math` cascade through the entire graph. Changes to `config` only rebuild `config` and `main`.

### Cycle Detection

```
ERROR: circular dependency detected
  src/auth.xi → src/database.xi → src/auth.xi
  
  Fix: extract shared types into a separate module
  that both auth and database import.
```

### Optimizing the Graph

```xiom
// BAD: tight coupling, deep chains
module app;
use app.auth.database.sql;  // 4 levels deep

// GOOD: shallow, focused dependencies
module app;
use shared.types;
use auth.session;
use db.pool;
```

### Dependency Analysis

```sh
xiom graph --stats
```

Output:
```
Modules: 47
Edges (dependencies): 89
Max depth: 5
Critical path: math → crypto → auth → api → main
Parallelizable: 12 modules (can build simultaneously)
Cycles: 0 (healthy)
```

### Build Order

The compiler topologically sorts modules and builds dependencies before dependents. Independent modules (no shared edges) are built in parallel.
syntax_ref:
xiom graph              # Generate dependency graph
xiom graph --stats      # Show graph statistics
xiom graph --cycles     # Check for circular deps
tips: Keep the dependency graph SHALLOW — deep chains mean slow rebuilds when base modules change
Extract shared types to a leaf module — everything depends on it, so it should be stable and small
Use `xiom graph --cycles` to catch circular dependencies before they cause build failures
Parallelizable modules are those with no dependencies between them — maximize these
common_mistakes: Creating circular dependencies — split shared code into a separate module
Making a core module depend on leaf modules — inverts the dependency direction
Not checking the graph regularly — dependency creep makes builds progressively slower
